newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - Nov 7.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average jumped more than 50 points Wednesday as Wall Street took comfort from the re-election of President Clinton and the Republicans' retaining control of Congress.
At 11:26 a.m. EST, the Dow was up 50.32 points at 6,131.50, which activated the New York Stock Exchange's limits on program trading.
The Dow tripped curbs on index-arbitrage trading at the New York Stock Exchange. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index also jumped, rising two to 342.

Analysts said they believed the division of power in Washington was the best course. Republicans in Congress keeping the Democrat president in check was a better scenario than the Democrats controlling two branches of the federal government, which might have led to increased spending.

Analysts also said the split was preferable to Bob Dole winning the presidency, since many Wall Street economists thought the Republicans would have failed to find spending cuts to match their proposed tax cuts.

"This is probably the least inflationary course that could have been taken, so there's lots of optimism," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at Boston-based PanAgora Asset Management Inc. "Everyone's happy. The Street is very comfortable with the idea of a Republican Congress keeping spending down."

LONDON - The UK stock market hit its lowest level in six weeks, as weak futures prices and worries about interest rates and U.S. elections weighed on prices. The FTSE 100 share index ended the day at 3,921.1 points, down 7.0 points on the day and
just 10 points off the day's low, as investors ignored firm gilts, a solid start on Wall Street and strong bourse performances across much of Europe.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade at the day's highs, boosted by stronger German Bunds. Bunds jumped on reports that Russian president Boris Yeltsin's heart operation was sucessfully completed and after German industry orders data came in below expectations. The 30-share DAX closed up 19.43 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,691.29. In post-bourse trade, the index was up 37.43 at 2,716.16.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply higher, but below the year's high, as bonds rallied and the market sighed relief after Yeltsin's heart surgery. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 45.17 points or 2.11 percent at 2,187.32.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed just off the day's highs in relatively high volume trade as foreign buying, a firmer U.S. dollar and higher Wall Street stocks bolstered prices. The all-share Swiss Performance Index advanced 17.41 points, or 0.72 percent, to close at 2,426.59.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed lower, after languishing in negative territory for most of the day. Trading was spiritless before U.S. elections and the launch of a new Japanese government and its policies. The key Nikkei 225 average fell 40.73 points, or 0.20 percent, to close at 20,592.33.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks fell sharply just before the close to end down on pre-U.S. election jitters and swift profit-taking from local and overseas institutions. The Hang Seng Index dropped 56.70 points in the last 15 minutes of
trading to close at 12,502.70, wiping away a 57-point gain to an all-time intraday high of 12,616.37 at mid-morning.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed slightly firmer in lacklustre trade after spending the day rangebound as market participants watched the Melbourne Cup and awaited the Reserve Bank's verdict on interest rates. The All Ordinaries index added 4.1 points to close at 2,361.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended down after failing to convincingly recover from a wave of futures-selling early in the day. Gold ended firm, but off the day's highs, on steadier bullion priced. Positive PPI data provided some support to stocks, but the market ignored finance minister Trevor Manuel's exchange control comments. The all-share index loses 28.9 points to end at 6,924.0 as industrials shed 26.9 points to close at 8,148.4. Gold rose 7.6 points to 1,740.1.
